text: Some friends of Day to Day also appear in that movie, "He's Just Not That Into You." The comic duo Frangela pop up here and there in the film, dishing out their take on love and relationships. Well, they came down to our studios earlier this week and spoke with my colleague Alex Cohen.
Angela Shelton and Frances Callier, welcome back.
Hello.
And congratulations, ladies.
Thank you.
Thank you.

Hollywood, big time. Now, I'm sure this is not going to come as a big surprise for our listeners. In this movie, apparently, you don't follow the script too much. You just kind of riff and speak on as you will.
Yes.
But now that you've seen the film, are you surprised at anything that actually made it in the final cut?
I was because - well, you know, there was a monologue. The part was originally just for one person, and we're always trying to argue people into letting us...
Yes.
Do things together, and it worked, for some reason, with these people.

And so, they let us do it together. So, we improvised around - I mean, there was a monologue there, but we gave some of our own, obviously, examples and input. So, we - you know, when we filmed, we filmed for a couple of hours, and we just didn't know what they had used.
Used, right.
So, I was really happy that a few of the lines that I really liked, that I wasn't sure they're going to make it in, did. So, that was cool. I don't want to blow 'em here.
Right, right.
Oh, come on, just a little preview?
Well, what we talk about is how to know when somebody is dumping you.
Right.
Because a lot of times, we miss the soft pass, the soft dump, you know, when somebody says something to you like, oh, I'm just going to be busy taking care of my own stuff for awhile.
Right, right, right. It's not you; it's me.
You know, that kind of stuff.
Yeah.
So, we go through a bunch of those. Like, lines with - that when you hear this, what you should hear is, I don't want to see you ever again.
Right.
That's what you need to hear.
Mm-hmm.
In this film, there's a couple of different types of women, shall we say. There's the woman who's been dating the same guy for seven years.
Yes.

And she's trying to get him to marry her; there's the woman who's frantically checking her phone 50 times a day, waiting for that guy to call. I'm just curious, if we can delve into your past, have you ever been that type of woman or a type of woman, Frances?
Oh, absolutely. I was - I have been the girl who was like, did he call? Did he call?
What did he - how did he sound? Well, it's just sort of a...
I have taken girlfriends on dates so that they can tell me what they saw. Is - does he look like is into me?
Well, that's the big check, isn't it?
Yes.
That's the big test. It's the best-friend test.
Yes.
You know, what does your best friend see when they see you with him?
So, Angela, it sounds like you're echoing this, but what kind of type were you? The anxious phone checker?

For me, you have to be really direct with me because otherwise, I don't understand. So, I don't know that people like me until they say, I am romantically attracted to you. Like, I don't get being hit on.
Because that's hot.
I know, but that's my - I'm, like, a Vulcan or something, like, I don't - Frances will tell you...
Yeah, yeah, yeah, you don't know.
People are hitting on me, and I have no idea they're hitting on me.
Angela has dated people that she had no idea that she was dating.
I was talking to a friend recently, and I was like, I didn't date in high school. She was like, you had a boyfriend all through high school, Angela. I was like, who?

And she was like, David. I was like, David wasn't my boyfriend. She was like, what did you guys do together? I said, well, I mean, every weekend, we'd, like, to go to the movies and hang out, and we made out, but I mean, and I was like, oh.
Yeah, that's called dating.
That was my boyfriend.
I really had no idea. And then I had to, like, email him on Facebook or - you know, and I was like, David, was that - were you my boyfriend? And he was like, ah, yeah.

So, let's fast forward a little bit. You're adults now, and I'd like to get, maybe, a little bit of your wisdom here. Everyone has been talking about the economy, and I'm curious if you've seen any reflections of the current financial turmoil in the world of dating and relationships. And Frances, you've been out of the dating scene for awhile, we should note; you are happily married.
Happily.
How is the economy, which is not so happy, affecting your relationship?
Our romance or so? You know, I think that, you know, we do a little role-playing. I play the tired, overworked mother.
He plays the misunderstood husband, and we play - we give each other in trade, like, clean laundry for sexy time.
Well, there is - there's not as much champagne. You guys used to have a lot of champagne brunches. Not so many champagne brunches.
Oh, yeah, we did. Not so many anymore.
Now, you have to make that Kool-Aid seem - just shake it up a little, you know...
Or find something that's fermented in the refrigerator...
And hope that you get a buzz from licking it. Like prison booze...
Yes.
Prison booze, basically, in your toilet.
Martha Stewart, I've never heard that one from her.
Well, she's got to start that.
Thanks, guys. And Angela, we will note here, you are still out there...
Yes, yes.
In the wonderful world of dating. What's it like in this economy?
Well, what I'm noticing is - well, a lot of restaurants are closing, unfortunately.
But couldn't you say, hey, this could be a good thing, because now you don't have to deal with the whole bill, like, do we split it?
Right.
Does he pay? Or is there a silver-lining kind of thing here?
No, no. I would rather go out to dinner, no.
Well, you know, you feel bad, too, because it's, like, trying to figure out a nice night out that isn't exactly McDonald's drive-thru.
Right, where you bring your own candles and tablecloth.
Right, and you just do it in the parking lot.
Yes.
Isn't this a lovely meal, so beautiful. Would you like sweet and sour with your McNuggets?
Angela Shelton and Frances Callier are Frangela. The comedy duo lives and loves here in Los Angeles. Thanks, ladies.
Thank you.
Thank you.
That's my colleague Alex Cohen, love that music. You can see Frangela in the movie "He's Just Not That Into You." There's more to come on Day to Day from NPR News.
